key_insight: A pseudostress-based fully mixed finite element method couples porous-solid deformation, fluid flow, electrostatics, and ionic transport while retaining poroelastic stability near incompressibility.
engineering_relevance: The method supports simulation of charged, saturated, deformable porous media with direct approximations of stresses, fluxes, and concentration gradients.
method: Reformulate mechanics using non-symmetric pseudostress and displacement, with mixed Darcy, electrostatic, and ionic equations.
Use conforming Raviart–Thomas elements and discontinuous polynomials, with algebraic reconstruction of displacement gradients and Cauchy stress.
Guide adaptive refinement with a residual-based a posteriori error estimator for the coupled 2D scheme.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports error estimates and numerical studies of convergence, near-incompressible robustness, adaptive refinement, and ionic polarization, without quantitative results.
watch_item: Well-posedness requires block stability and small-data assumptions; estimator reliability needs an additional smallness condition, and general boundary traces require oscillation terms.
paper_title: A pseudostress-based fully mixed finite element method for the stationary Biot--Poisson--Nernst--Planck system
